meta: Estimate your MEPCO bill from units with the 2026 NEPRA slabs, fixed charge, QTA, GST and the latest NEPRA FPA. South Punjab summer bills explained.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the MEPCO per unit rate?
p: MEPCO bills the uniform A-1 domestic tariff that NEPRA determined and the Government notified for 2026; there is no separate MEPCO tariff. An unprotected home in Multan, Bahawalpur or Rahim Yar Khan pays the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: 400 units are all billed at Rs 36.46. Each slab is dearer than the one below, and the open-ended top slab is the most expensive.

Protected consumers are billed slab by slab at two low rates, and lifeline consumers lower still. The table below prints the rate for each slab from the tariff file, and the worked examples cover a winter month, a one-AC summer month, a two-AC summer month and a month with the FPA entered.

sections.h2: MEPCO summer vs winter units: why the June bill is many times the January bill
p: South Punjab has long, hot summers, so from May to September the AC does most of the consumption. A split inverter AC of one and a half tons draws up to about 1,450 W and a non-inverter one about 1,800 W, so eight to ten hours a night adds a few hundred units. The slab the month reaches then applies to every unit, which is why the summer bill grows faster than the units do.

In the examples, the winter month of 120 units stays protected at Rs 2,727, the one-AC summer month of 400 units costs Rs 20,894, and the two-AC month of 750 units costs Rs 49,303. Use the AC units calculator to estimate your own summer units before entering them here.

sections.h2: What is the FPA line on a MEPCO bill?
p: FPA is the fuel price adjustment: a per-unit amount NEPRA sets each month for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs to pass on the difference between the fuel cost assumed in the tariff and the actual cost. It can be a charge or a credit, and it is applied to the units of the month named on the bill. Because it is set after the month ends, this calculator pre-fills the latest NEPRA-verified month; copy the current rate from the bill into the FPA field under advanced settings.
GST is charged on the subtotal including the FPA, so a positive FPA also raises the GST line. The fourth worked example shows the effect on 400 units.

sections.h2: MEPCO bill check vs this MEPCO bill estimate
p: This page estimates the bill from the units, sanctioned load and category you enter. The official MEPCO bill, with the reference number, due date, arrears and the exact FPA, is on the MEPCO website, which links the online bill check on the PITC portal; enter the reference number from the top of any earlier bill there. Use the estimate to see what each printed line should be and to plan the summer months.

If a bill looks too high, compare its units with the reading dates first: a cycle longer than a month can push the units into a higher slab. The bill audit tool checks that for you. Every bill also carries an FPA line; see what the FPA line on your bill means. A home on a time-of-use meter can check the peak hours for MEPCO.

The south Punjab districts around Multan, run through zones in Multan, Khanewal, Sahiwal, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rahim Yar Khan and Vehari. If your bill carries another company's name, use that company's calculator.

faq.q: How do I get a MEPCO bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and the sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FPA with the one on your bill under advanced settings. For 400 units on 2 kW the estimate is Rs 20,894, FPA included.

faq.q: What is the MEPCO per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab the month reaches: Rs 36.46 per unit for an unprotected home using 400 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: Is the MEPCO tariff the same as other DISCOs?
faq.a: Yes. The 2026 tariff notified as SRO 279(I)/2026 is uniform for all ex-WAPDA DISCOs and K-Electric. NEPRA sets one FPA for every DISCO too, so a MEPCO bill for the same units equals a LESCO bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: How many units does an AC add to a MEPCO summer bill?
faq.a: A one and a half ton inverter AC draws up to about 1,450 W, less once the room is cool, so a night of eight to ten hours adds several units a day and a few hundred a month. The AC units calculator gives a figure for your tonnage and hours.

MEPCO covers thirteen districts of south Punjab: Multan, Khanewal, Lodhran, Vehari, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Rahim Yar Khan, Muzaffargarh, Layyah, Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur. Faults and billing complaints go to the national electricity helpline 118 (call, or SMS 8118).

faq.q: How do I check my MEPCO bill online?
faq.a: The MEPCO website links an online bill check on the PITC portal; enter the reference number printed at the top of an earlier bill, digits only, to see the current bill. This calculator estimates the bill from units; it does not fetch your account.

faq.q: Why is my MEPCO bill higher than this estimate?
faq.a: The estimate uses the pre-filled FPA unless you enter your bill's, and it cannot see arrears, late payment surcharge or meter rent. A reading cycle longer than a month can also push the units into a higher slab; the bill audit tool checks that.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: MEPCO, the Multan Electric Power Company, supplies south Punjab from Multan through zones in Khanewal, Sahiwal, Bahawalpur, Bahawalnagar, Muzaffargarh, Dera Ghazi Khan, Rahim Yar Khan and Vehari, and bills the uniform NEPRA A-1 domestic tariff for 2026 rather than a tariff of its own.
An unprotected MEPCO consumer using 400 units pays Rs 36.46 on every unit, which is Rs 14,584 of energy charge before the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA and GST.
A south Punjab summer month of 400 units with one inverter AC costs about Rs 20,894, while the same home's protected winter month of 120 units costs about Rs 2,727.

The FPA on a MEPCO bill is a per-unit figure that changes every month; on 400 units the FPA entered in the fourth example adds Rs 1,000 before GST, which is why two months with the same units can total differently.
A MEPCO protected consumer is one whose last 6 bills were all at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; the first AC month of summer usually ends that run.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,480 to the bill of an unprotected 2 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Expecting a MEPCO tariff that differs from Lahore or Karachi. The slab rates are the uniform NEPRA rates; only the monthly FPA is specific to the month.
Estimating the summer from a winter bill. In south Punjab the AC months reach a far higher slab, and every unit of the month is billed at that slab's rate.
Ticking protected after the first AC month. One bill over 200 units moves the home to unprotected rates for the next 6 months.
Keeping the pre-filled FPA when the bill shows a different one. GST is charged on the FPA too, so an FPA that differs from your bill's moves the GST line as well.

fields.hint: The kW printed in the connection details of the MEPCO bill. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FPA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

examples.text: Fans and lights only: energy charge Rs 1,314 slab-wise at protected rates, fixed charge Rs 300 for 1 kW, FC surcharge Rs 388, QTA Rs 62, FPA Rs 247, GST Rs 416. Estimated MEPCO bill Rs 2,727.

examples.title: 400 units, summer month with one inverter AC
examples.text: All 400 units at Rs 36.46 = Rs 14,584, fixed charge Rs 800 for 2 kW, FC surcharge Rs 1,292, QTA Rs 208, FPA Rs 823, GST Rs 3,187. Estimated MEPCO bill Rs 20,894.

examples.title: 750 units, two ACs in a Multan June, 3 kW connection
examples.text: The month reaches the open-ended top slab, so all 750 units are billed at Rs 47.20 = Rs 35,400, fixed charge Rs 2,025 for 3 kW, FC surcharge Rs 2,423, QTA Rs 390, FPA Rs 1,544, GST Rs 7,521. Estimated MEPCO bill Rs 49,303.

examples.text: Same 400 units as the second example, energy charge Rs 14,584 and fixed charge Rs 800, but the FPA adds Rs 1,000 to the subtotal of Rs 17,884 and GST becomes Rs 3,219. Estimated MEPCO bill Rs 21,103 including the FPA.

content.answer: A MEPCO home in Multan or anywhere in south Punjab using 400 units in a summer month as an unprotected consumer on a 2 kW connection pays about Rs 20,894: Rs 14,584 energy charge at Rs 36.46 per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FPA and GST. MEPCO bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + surcharges, then GST.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC, QTA, FPA = per-unit surcharges printed on the MEPCO bill
